OFFICIAL STATEMENT 

Philippine Accessible Disability Services Inc. (PADS)

On the Mockery, Mimicking, and Degrading Portrayal of Persons with Disabilities for Entertainment and Social Media Content

The Philippine Accessible Disability Services Inc. (PADS) strongly condemns the acts of making fun of, imitating, and mimicking the gestures, movements, and conditions of persons with disabilities (PWDs) for entertainment, publicity, or social media engagement.

Disability is not a joke. Human dignity is not entertainment.

The everyday struggles, physical limitations, communication barriers, and social challenges experienced by persons with disabilities are real. They are not props for comedy, punchlines for television, or content material to generate views, likes, and online popularity.

We are deeply concerned when television personalities, reality show participants, and content creators use their influence and platforms to normalize behavior that humiliates, stereotypes, and undermines the dignity of persons with disabilities. Public figures, producers, and content creators must understand that their actions carry influence and consequences.

THE LAW MUST BE UPHELD

We emphasize that the Philippines has existing laws that protect persons with disabilities against public ridicule and vilification.

Republic Act No. 7277, otherwise known as the Magna Carta for Persons with Disabilities, as amended by Republic Act No. 9442, explicitly prohibits making fun of, contemptuously imitating, or mocking persons with disabilities because of their impairments.

Its Implementing Rules and Regulations specifically identify the imitation of persons with disabilities in television shows, broadcast media, stage performances, and other forms of entertainment, when offensive to their rights and dignity, as acts of public ridicule.

Under Section 46 of RA 7277, as amended by RA 9442, violators may face the following penalties:

* First violation: A fine of ₱50,000 to ₱100,000, imprisonment of six months to two years, or both, at the discretion of the court.
* Subsequent violations: A fine of ₱100,000 to ₱200,000, imprisonment of two to six years, or both, at the discretion of the court.

Furthermore, when the violator is a corporation, organization, or similar entity, officials directly involved may also be held liable under the law.

We therefore call on the appropriate authorities to determine the circumstances, investigate the incidents, and pursue the appropriate legal action wherever warranted. Accountability must not be compromised simply because the individuals involved are celebrities, public personalities, or influential content creators.

OUR CALL TO THE ENTERTAINMENT INDUSTRY

We urge television networks, program producers, directors, creative teams, and digital content platforms to exercise greater sensitivity, responsibility, and accountability in producing and distributing entertainment content.

The entertainment industry has an enormous influence in shaping public attitudes and social behavior. With that influence comes the responsibility to protect the dignity of marginalized sectors.

We strongly encourage producers to institutionalize disability-sensitivity orientations, review their creative content, and establish safeguards against discriminatory and degrading portrayals of persons with disabilities.

Entertainment should never come at the expense of another person’s dignity.

OUR CALL TO GOVERNMENT AND LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES

We urge the National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA), the Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB), the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), the Philippine National Police (PNP), local Persons with Disability Affairs Offices (PDAOs), and other concerned government agencies to strictly enforce existing laws and regulations.
